comparator.name: Economie en Bedrijfseconomie
comparator.sourceNotes: Verified on 27 October 2026 against the current programme page and adopted TiSEM EER v4, pp61–64, for the 2026 entrant cohort. The Dutch full-time bachelor has 180 EC. Both formal branches are equally broad; the neutral official-order tie-break selects Bedrijfseconomie. Required common and branch-specific courses are retained. Financiële Administratie (324928-B-6) is the selected 6-EC restricted elective. The 30-EC approved mobility/minor window remains unspecified. GROW is zero-credit extracurricular development; later semesters explicitly describe it as noncompulsory and strongly recommended. EER3.7 governs choice-space approval and nonoverlap. Article4.5 requires120EC for the sixth-semester thesis,138EC from semester7 and90EC for internship,with applicable manual/syllabus requirements. The positive BSA threshold is42first-yearEC;Article4.4 governs postponed-BSA progression. Article4.7 permits attendance conditions for assessed practical exercises,announced in OSIRIS/Canvas.

alternatives.labelRationale: Six economics courses and quantitative/qualitative methods form the core; political/legal institutions, civil society and sustainability governance apply that analysis to social policy. This does not claim specialised labour or housing economics.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the business-and-data option, this programme gives substantial weight to comparative politics, public and EU law, social theory, qualitative inquiry and sustainability governance. EU law supplies concrete analysis of market integration and the movement of workers, goods and establishments; these courses implement the evidenced economic-institutions direction.

alternatives.concept: Economics and practical financial decision-making are combined with econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and computational planning under uncertainty. Quantitative methods support economic and financial inquiry; they are not specialised asset-pricing or financial-risk courses.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the first programme, programming, relational databases, computational planning, linear algebra and advanced calculus replace experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product development, organisational psychology and market research. This is a real shift toward quantitative economic/financial inquiry; compared with the policy option, it retains business and financial foundations instead of the political/legal/social-policy strand.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three independently tested directions are retained:business/economics/data;economics with institutions and public policy;economics and practical finance with quantitative methods. The original policy composition is reconstructed because a Walcheren-expedition history seminar has no specific economic-policy contribution and Comparative Constitutional Law lacked its formal gateway. Related theory and mathematics supply concrete foundations. Finance remains a methods-rich economics direction,not a complete specialist finance degree. notes.text: Tilburg requires a combined economics-and-business curriculum, a 24-EC specialisation and a 12-EC thesis. The displayed external route is Bedrijfseconomie. The UCR options differ in business, data and public-policy emphasis and do not reproduce specialised management accounting, business administration, company law or sustainable finance. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Economie en Bedrijfseconomie at Tilburg University combines economic theory, accounting, finance, business and data analysis. Students choose an Economics or Business Economics specialisation after the common first year. This comparison shows the Dutch-language Bedrijfseconomie route.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options combine economics with business and data, public institutions and social policy, or practical finance and quantitative methods. Tilburg retains a more specialised accounting and business-economics sequence and a required 12-EC thesis. Shared rows show partial content relationships, not course equivalence.
